title: 🌏 Auckland Asian Networking Night
description:
Looking to meet new people, expand your professional network, or simply enjoy meaningful conversations over a drink?

Auckland Asian Networking Night is a relaxed community meetup inspired by Auckland's diverse Asian community, bringing together people from all backgrounds to connect, share experiences, and build genuine relationships.

You don't have to be Asian to join. If you enjoy meeting people from diverse backgrounds and appreciate Asian cultures, you're more than welcome.

No presentations. No formal agenda. Just good conversations.

👥 WHO'S THIS FOR?
Whether you're:

* A professional from any industry
* An entrepreneur or small business owner
* A freelancer or creative
* A student or working holiday maker
* Looking for a new career opportunity
* Or simply interested in meeting new people

💬 WHAT TO EXPECT
Grab a drink, introduce yourself, and join any conversation that interests you.

There's no fixed seating, no scheduled activities, and no pressure. Simply move around, meet different people, and enjoy conversations at your own pace.

You might leave with:

* New friends
* Professional connections
* Career insights
* Business opportunities
* Collaboration ideas
* Or simply a great evening with interesting people

Most people attend on their own, so don't worry if you're coming solo. We'll help you feel welcome.

📍 EVENT DETAILS

* Location: Mixed 1981 Cafe, 50 Fort St, Auckland CBD, Auckland
* Time: 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM (feel free to arrive a little earlier to grab a drink)
* Frequency: Every two weeks
* Capacity: Limited spaces available
* Entry: $10 per person, FREE for Hanahub members (Free to sign up at [hanahub.co.nz](https://www.hanahub.co.nz/))

☕ This event is proudly sponsored by Mixed 1981. All attendees are required to purchase at least one drink, and Hanahub members enjoy a drink discount, so simply show your profile on the night.

🍪 Korean snacks will be served on the night, so come and enjoy a taste of Korea while you mingle.

🎒 WHAT TO BRING

title: EMC English Conversation Club
description:
**EMC English Conversation Club**
**Thursdays, 4 to 6pm**
**Free.** Please **join this group** and **reserve** your seat every week.

Whether you want to improve your English or you're a native speaker keen to help others, this is a great place to connect and build friendships.
This is not a classroom. It’s a relaxed community space where you can share stories, practise everyday English, and learn about life, work, and culture in New Zealand and other countries.
Each session is guided by an experienced facilitator and supported by friendly volunteers.
**What to expect:**
• Casual, friendly conversations on real-life topics
• Supportive facilitators and volunteers
• Language learning through connection, not pressure
• A welcoming environment to build friendships and confidence

Please **join this group** and **reserve** your seat every week.

title: Beyond the Chat Window: Building a Real AI Workspace
description:
This session looks at what it takes to move beyond a single chat window and build a genuine AI workspace – a considered set of tools, habits, and workflows that support the way you actually work and live.

We'll map the landscape by category rather than by brand, so you can understand what each type of tool is for, where the boundaries between them sit, and how they fit together into something coherent.

The focus is practical and aimed at professionals, builders, operators, and anyone who has accumulated a scattering of AI subscriptions without a sense of how they connect – team leads and those setting direction for others will also find plenty to take away.

We'll explore-

* The categories that make up an AI workspace – conversational assistants, coding and agentic tools, automation and orchestration, knowledge capture, research and search, generation of images, audio and video, and where each genuinely earns its place.
* Choosing between frontier models, specialised tools, and local options – the trade-offs in capability, cost, privacy, and control.
* Connecting your tools to your context – files, notes, calendars, email, and codebases, and what changes when AI can actually see your work.
* Techniques that separate casual use from serious use – prompting patterns, structured context, reusable instructions, and knowing when to hand off a task versus do it yourself.
* Automation and agents – identifying which recurring work is worth automating, and recognising the tasks where supervision still matters more than speed.
* Extending the workspace into life beyond work – planning, learning, health, finances, household logistics, and creative projects.
* The cost of complexity – tool sprawl, subscription creep, fragile workflows, and how to keep a stack small enough to actually maintain.
* Privacy, data boundaries, and trust – deciding what you're willing to put where, and building sensible defaults.
